title: Precision limiter workshop notes — model compression and routing
body:
Context and objective:

Quick notes from the 2/11 cross-functional workshop with the retail customer (onsite) and field engineering: scope was to design a low-cost, latency-safe inference strategy for customer A's chat+search assistant for SKU lookup and conversational support. Goal: produce an experimental plan and concrete config candidates (model variants, quantization recipes, routing rules) to run a 2-week lab POC.

Top-level constraints we have to satisfy (customer requirements):
- 95th percentile tail latency <= 240 ms for single-turn SKU lookups (95% of calls are short queries)
- Monthly token cost target: <= 40% of current cloud-hosted baseline (customer benchmarked with a large proprietary model)
- Sensitive PII: must stay on private deployment for labeled flows (10% of traffic).
- Quality floor: retrieval+generation answers must maintain entity recall >= 92% (measured on their 3.5k test prompts).

High-level approach proposed (summary):
1) Two-stage cascade + policy-based routing: cheap fast model for short, high-confidence queries; larger model fallthrough for low-confidence / long prompts.
2) Aggressive quantization on small/medium tiers (INT8/AWQ) with conservative quantization for large backends (GPTQ-4bit only if tuned).
3) KV/prefix caching for repeated SKU phrases + request-level prompt slimming (strip metadata when eligible).
4) Canary rollout via dedicated pool with capacity reserve and fallback to hosted models for non-sensitive traffic.

Model selection candidates (rationales and initial test pairs):
- Tier A (fast, cheap): 7B transformer, distilled Mistral-like or Llama-7b-compat, optimized for short-context generation. Why: good token-efficiency and low mem footprint => allows high qps. Plan: test with AWQ-int8 and GPTQ-4bit baselines (both).
- Tier B (mid): 13B LLM (Mistral 13B / Llama2-13B-Chat variant). Why: better factuality for entity recall with moderate latency. Test with fp16 and int8 fallback.
- Tier C (backstop): 33B+ or hosted high-quality clone (customer accepts hosted fallback for non-sensitive traffic). Use fp16 and selective 8-bit for attention kernels only.

Quantization and compression notes (experiments to run):
- AWQ (post-training quant with per-channel scaling) on Tier A: expected ~2.5-3x speedup on AMP-enabled GPUs; measure quality drop on SKU retrieval prompts specifically.
- GPTQ 4-bit with layerwise tuning on Tier A: more aggressive, may produce hallucination spikes on entity-heavy prompts — test with 1k prompt sweep.
- Smooth-quant (symmetric per-tensor) on Tier B as low-risk middle ground.
- Mixed-precision kernels for Tier C (fp16 key/kv, int8 matmul where validated) to keep latency in range.
- Small-weights-sparsity experiment (8-12% structured pruning) — low priority but plan a micro-benchmark for memory/latency wins.

Prompt and pipeline heuristics (practical rules we sketched):
- Prompt slimming: automatic removal of non-critical system metadata if token_count > 250 AND intent=lookup. Keep a short trace for auditing.
- Intent classifier upfront (tiny binary classifier, ~50ms): route to SKU lookup pipeline vs. general regen. This reduces calls to Tier B/C by ~45% in similar customers.
- Prefix KV caching: store past SKU descriptions keyed by normalized SKU+customer-region. TTL 36 hours by default, evict LRU. Cache hit -> use template-based filler + small LLM post-edit.
- Confidence gating: use calibrated model score + n-gram match to decide whether to accept Tier A output or escalate. Conservative threshold tuned to meet 92% recall.

Routing & deployment rules (practical):
- Sensitive flows always pinned to Private deployment (VPC) and never sent to hosted fallback. Non-sensitive can be routed by cost/latency policy.
- Primary routing policy: latency SLO first (if expected latency for Tier A < 120ms and confidence high -> keep). Fallback policy: if capacity exhausted, send to hosted Tier C for non-sensitive traffic, else queued with a short wait-and-retry (150ms).
- Autoscaling targets: Tier A pool scaled to 600 qps baseline for retail peak; reserve headroom 20% for burst.

Telemetry & measurements to collect during POC:
- Token-level cost per model variant, median/95/99 latency by model and route, end-to-end retrieval+generation entity recall and precision, top-1 hallucination rate (entity fabrication).
- Confusion matrix for intent classifier; false negative rate is critical (missed lookups -> up-route).
- Cache hit rate, average TTL eviction latency, cache staleness incidents.

Immediate action items (owners + due dates):
- Aisha: Assemble 1k prompt sweep set from customer logs (anonymized) — DUE 2025-02-14.
- Miguel: Stand up Tier A container images with AWQ and GPTQ toolchain; produce perf baseline on g5x2 and a100-slim — DUE 2025-02-17.
- Claire: Implement tiny intent classifier prototype (binary) and mount as pre-filter in the test harness; provide calibration script — DUE 2025-02-16.
- Jonah: Design routing config prototypes (policy table + fallback rules) and simulate traffic for 48h using recorded distribution — DUE 2025-02-18.
- SE team: Add telemetry guards in console dashboard for 95/99 latency SLO alerts and cost-per-token trending — DUE 2025-02-20.

Risks & open questions (needs triage):
- Quality regression on AWQ/GPTQ for entity-heavy prompts. Mitigation: label-oriented evals and quick rollback to fp16.
- Cache staleness and TTL semantics for SKU updates — need customer's update cadence and invalidation hooks.
- Private deployment resource constraints: if their on-prem GPUs are older (A10-like), AWQ/GPTQ behavior will differ. Need hardware inventory.
- Intent classifier drift — schedule weekly re-eval if distribution changes.

Experiment matrix (short):
- Sweep A: Tier A (7B) x {fp16, AWQ-int8, GPTQ-4bit} x {no caching, caching} -> collect latency, recall, hallucination.
- Sweep B: Tier B (13B) x {fp16, int8-smooth} x {prompt-slimming ON/OFF} -> measure recall uplift and cost delta.
- Sweep C: Full cascade latencies with routing thresholds {0.6,0.7,0.8} confidence -> find point where token-reduction meets recall target.

Success criteria for POC:
- Meet latency SLO (95th <= 240ms) across 90% of traffic distribution sample.
- Token cost reduction >= 35% vs baseline while preserving recall >= 92% on labeled set.
- No PII leakage incidents and private flow isolation confirmed by audit logs.

Measuring quality without chasing perfection: prioritization suggestion from workshop:
- First run: focus on SKU lookup subset (1k prompts) for quality and latency.
- Second run: expand to mixed dialog (2k prompts) and test prompt slimming impact.
- Fail fast: if AWQ causes recall dip > 4 pts on SKU set, revert to fp16+slimming for Tier A.

Notes from breakouts (raw, candid):
- Miguel: "GPTQ 4-bit produced sporadic entity swap on 7B when we forced longer completions — looks like attention scaling artifact."
- Claire: "Intent classifier false negatives mostly come from multi-sentence user messages; adding a short sentence-split preprocessor reduced FN by 35%."
- Aisha: "Customer is open to short caching TTL if it lowers cost, but they want a rollback hook tied to product catalog updates."

Proposed timeline (2-week lab):
- Day 0–2: data prep (anonymize logs, build evaluation sets), infra baseline.
- Day 3–7: run Sweep A and Sweep B, gather metrics, quick analysis.
- Day 8–10: tuning (confidence thresholds, prompt slimming heuristics), run cascade sim.
- Day 11–13: deploy canary in dedicated pool, run live traffic at 5–10% weight.
- Day 14: final analysis, decision memo for customer (go/no-go).

Decision memo outline to customer (one-pager):
- Executive summary of recommended config (Tier A: 7B AWQ-int8 + intent prefilter + cache; Tier B: 13B fp16; Tier C: hosted fallback for non-sensitive).
- Measured tradeoffs (latency, cost, recall) from lab.
- Migration steps and rollback playbook.
- Next steps & commercial ask (Dedicated sizing request / Private deployment checklist).

Appendix (quick reference):
- Quick commands: AWQ conversion script: ./tools/awq_quantize --model <model-dir> --out <out-dir> --per-channel
- Baseline perf targets to hit on a g5x2: Tier A median < 65ms, 95th < 130ms.
- Calibration notebook: GH-PR-4523 (internal).

Endnotes / follow-ups planned:
- Collect customer's hardware inventory and catalog update cadence (action: SE engagement lead).
- Add a small human-in-the-loop check for first 48 hours of canary traffic on sensitive flows.
- Schedule a review call with product-hosted-api and infra teams to validate capacity assumptions (tentative 2/21).

Raw thought: keep the cascade simple to start — avoid 4+ tier networks until we have stable confidence scoring. Complexity kills observability and increases debugging time during customer trials.

-- Aisha (workshop lead)
